contracts.name: NLA.IE02.coefficient_roundtrip
contracts.independent_reasoning: The finite coefficient sum is inverse to the exponent-two coefficient vector; high coefficients are excluded only with the stated degree bound. Dimension zero and the zero polynomial are retained.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.coefficient_inner_product
contracts.independent_reasoning: The sum is the actual complex Euclidean inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument. It is not merely equality of real parts.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.toeplitz_action
contracts.independent_reasoning: The explicit lower diagonal entries give exactly coefficient convolution followed by truncation; finite-index arithmetic includes empty dimensions.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.toeplitz_algebra
contracts.independent_reasoning: The matrix polynomial algebra map preserves addition, multiplication, scalars and identity. Nilpotent shift truncates precisely at n; multiplication order and finite inverse consumers agree.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.nilpotent_inverse
contracts.independent_reasoning: The supplied nonzero scalar and zero constant coefficient give a nilpotent remainder. A finite geometric sum proves both inverse orders, with no inverse oracle or convergence assumption.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.euclidean_norm_attainment
contracts.independent_reasoning: The operator norm is genuinely attained on the nonempty Euclidean unit sphere in positive dimension, using compactness and continuity.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.maximal_space_norm
contracts.independent_reasoning: The Gram-operator kernel is equivalent to equality in the true operator norm bound. The zero vector is handled separately; the nonzero case uses the self-adjoint Rayleigh extremum.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.schur_diagonal_bound
contracts.independent_reasoning: A coordinate of the action on a unit basis vector bounds the constant diagonal coefficient by the operator norm.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.schur_scalar_endpoint
contracts.independent_reasoning: When the diagonal coefficient has unit norm, the finite first-column square sum forces every remaining visible coefficient to vanish. Only proof-quality finding Q1 applies.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.schur_dimension_one
contracts.independent_reasoning: The one-dimensional endpoint supplies the complete scalar Schur pair and its maximal-space dimension, rather than assuming interpolation.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.schur_defect_identity
contracts.independent_reasoning: The exact adjoint expansion gives the stated signed defect identity; the real scalar 1-|c|^2 and conjugations are consistent.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.schur_strict_reduction
contracts.independent_reasoning: Strict diagonal modulus supplies a two-sided finite inverse. The energy identity gives contractivity and an actual norm-attaining vector gives boundary norm one for the reduced matrix.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.schur_active_block
contracts.independent_reasoning: The shifted active block removes the leading zero output and trailing input coordinate exactly; both norm directions and Toeplitz structure are proved.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.schur_pair_step
contracts.independent_reasoning: All eleven clauses of the larger supplied-data Schur pair are proved, including degrees, disk denominator nonvanishing, coprimality, interpolation, full kernel description, action and finrank.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.finite_schur_boundary
contracts.independent_reasoning: Induction strictly decreases n, with scalar/unit endpoints. Existence of Schur data and the entire maximal kernel are established without a Schur or Caratheodory-Fejer oracle.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.scaled_maximal_factorization
contracts.independent_reasoning: Positive operator norm is divided out and then restored. The scale, maximal kernel and complex action all use the actual matrix norm.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.reflection_algebra
contracts.independent_reasoning: Fixed-bound reflection and conjugation agree with Mathlib reflect; its behavior above the bound is explicitly controlled by the hypotheses.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.reflection_product
contracts.independent_reasoning: The reflected product uses the sum of the two valid degree bounds. No unjustified general multiplicativity of reflection above its bound is used.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.reflection_evaluation
contracts.independent_reasoning: On the nonzero unit circle, reciprocal conjugation and the degree power produce the exact evaluation identity.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.circle_polynomial_uniqueness
contracts.independent_reasoning: The complex unit circle is proved infinite via an injective upper semicircle parameterization; equality at infinitely many points then gives polynomial equality.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.weighted_fold
contracts.independent_reasoning: For every nonnegative weight, real square root scaling multiplies the squared complex norm by that weight, including zero weights.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.common_circle_root_reduction
contracts.independent_reasoning: Vanishing of a sum of nonnegative squares forces a common root. Each polynomial is divided by the same linear factor; the degree parameter decreases only after proving it positive.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.fourier_semantics
contracts.independent_reasoning: Finite coefficient expansion gives the u-v frequency sign, conjugate symmetry, the degree band, and the evaluation identity. Nonzero input supplies a positive zero coefficient.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.effective_factor_polynomial
contracts.independent_reasoning: The actual maximal nonzero Fourier frequency ell controls both extreme coefficients and degree 2*ell, self reflection and unit-circle evaluation. The ell=0 case is retained.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.reciprocal_root_pairing
contracts.independent_reasoning: All roots are a multiset, preserving multiplicity. Reciprocal conjugation pairs roots after excluding zero and unit-circle roots from the strict positive circle data.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.reciprocal_inside_factor
contracts.independent_reasoning: Inside and outside root multisets are complementary and equally sized. The complete complex factorization has the exact degree and scalar, including empty roots.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.strict_scalar_factorization
contracts.independent_reasoning: The complex proportionality scalar is evaluated at z=1 and proved positive real before taking its square root. The resulting polynomial has the required degree and all-circle squared norm identity.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.weighted_scalar_factorization
contracts.independent_reasoning: Induction removes every common circle factor; the strictly positive remainder uses the full root factorization. Zero/empty families and zero weights are included.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.weighted_coefficient_preservation
contracts.independent_reasoning: Coefficient extraction of fixed-degree reflected products preserves every full complex pairing, not only squared norms or real parts; truncation handles high-degree directions.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.maximal_complex_preservation
contracts.independent_reasoning: The full Schur kernel representation and weighted factorization construct one unit maximal vector preserving all complex directional inner products simultaneously.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.gradient_compact_convex
contracts.independent_reasoning: The actual gradient image of the compact nonempty unit maximal set is compact; direct two-point preservation proves real convexity of that image itself, without substituting a convex hull.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.real_separator_complex_form
contracts.independent_reasoning: A real continuous functional on complex coordinates is represented with coefficients ell(e_j)-i*ell(i*e_j). This matches the inner product convention and later descent sign.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.gradient_strict_separation
contracts.independent_reasoning: If zero is absent, strict separation of the actual closed compact convex image yields one complex direction and a uniformly positive real margin.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.half_certificate
contracts.independent_reasoning: The exact positive-half statement is proved by the one explicit interval_decide invocation in kernel mode and is consumed in the descent positivity proof.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.descent_step_bounds
contracts.independent_reasoning: The explicit half-times-minimum steps are positive and bounded by one and the required ratios. All denominators contain positive +1 terms; no numerical subdivision is used.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.descent_quadratic_expansion
contracts.independent_reasoning: The real quadratic norm expansion has the negative 2*epsilon cross term and correct epsilon^2 contribution, matching T-epsilon*D.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.descent_complement_gap
contracts.independent_reasoning: A gap is extracted only when the compact complement is nonempty, from a genuine maximum strictly below the maximal norm value.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.descent_empty_complement
contracts.independent_reasoning: The independent empty-complement step uses uniform positive directional forms on the sphere; it does not invoke a maximum of an empty set.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.descent_nonempty_complement
contracts.independent_reasoning: The positive gap controls low-form vectors and the margin controls high-form vectors, with both estimates valid for the same explicit step.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.positive_gradient_descent
contracts.independent_reasoning: The two complement cases produce strict operator-norm decrease by applying the unit-vector estimate at an actual norm-attaining vector.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.minimizer_orthogonality
contracts.independent_reasoning: A nonzero minimizing Toeplitz residual cannot have a gradient image excluding zero: the actual strict descent would contradict its minimizing property. The perturbation coefficient sign is -epsilon*c.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.affine_operator_minimum
contracts.independent_reasoning: Finite linear-combination range is a closed finite-dimensional subspace of continuous linear maps with the actual operator norm; nearest-point existence supplies an attained infimum even with dependent directions.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.affine_vector_minimum
contracts.independent_reasoning: The same finite-dimensional nearest-point argument in the actual Euclidean vector space gives an attained inner minimum for every vector, including zero. Only proof-quality finding Q2 applies.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.affine_minimax_attained
contracts.independent_reasoning: Zero residual and positive residual are separate. In the positive case, full complex orthogonality and Pythagoras provide one common worst vector and matching attained affine minima/maxima.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.jordan_reversal
contracts.independent_reasoning: The explicit reversal permutation is involutive and norm-preserving and conjugates the canonical upper Jordan block to the lower one; finite-index endpoint and empty-dimension cases are valid.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.jordan_direction_toeplitz
contracts.independent_reasoning: Every power of the lower Jordan block is a lower Toeplitz matrix by the already-proved algebra, with no restriction on the complex eigenvalue.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.normalized_polynomial_residuals
contracts.independent_reasoning: Every complex polynomial with degree at most k and constant value one is represented by precisely k free complex coefficients and conversely; k=0 is retained.

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.jordan_polynomial_transport

contracts.name: NLA.IE02.gmres_extrema_semantics
contracts.independent_reasoning: Actual sInf/sSup definitions are linked to attained norm minima/maxima by exact set-range equalities. Nonempty feasible sets and bounds prevent vacuous totalized extrema.

contracts.independent_reasoning: The theorem quantifies every n>=2, nonzero complex lam and 1<=k<n for the unchanged upper Jordan matrix, complex polynomials and complex vectors.
